about: The buildings' cases (plan-vector K10): close and far views where walls, cells and roofs decide the likeness, beyond the boards and sweeps of smoke.json. Near the Westerkerk (the bundled living map) a wall's ncol x nrow cells within 460 m, the Prinsengracht's houseboats drawn as boats on a moment with weather and as buildings on the living map's night, which has none; on the canal ring (the Main board's pack) its gables and roofs at a street's distance, straight down (every flat top seen from above), low over the roofs (pitch 70), and far (one cell a wall). Structural, engine mode, at S1; the full tier.

issues.name: melting buildings
issues.about: The renders paint whole items far to near by one point each (amsterdam.py's gatherItems: the footprint's centroid at half the height), so at some angles a farther building's walls are painted over a nearer one's and the buildings melt into each other (a tall building behind a long low one in front of it). The engine draws what stands up at its true depth (CP/shaders/shared/painter.slang) and does not copy this: where a case's frame differs from the port's because of it, the engine is right. Within a building the renders' order is kept where its faces touch (a later cell's edge over an earlier one's, a roof over the edge of its walls); faces of two buildings that touch meet where their geometry puts them. The painter switch (FrameOptions::painter) draws the renders' order, to compare; the owner maps are drawn under it. CP/tests/building/buildings_vk_test.cpp's melting pair shows both.
